summary: Two-part history of how fascism took root in Spain, from imperial collapse and Primo de Rivera's 1923 dictatorship to the Falange, and how Franco's Nationalists, backed by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, won the 1936-1939 Civil War.

evidence.note: 1898 loss to the US framed as the postcolonial trauma that starts the story
Anarcho-syndicalist unions, 1909 Barcelona general strike and its repression
Rif insurrection in northern Morocco and the 1921 rout of the Spanish army
Primo de Rivera's 1923 pronunciamiento in Barcelona sets up military dictatorship
Spanish and French forces use poison gas on Rif civilians
Dictatorship falls in 1930, Second Republic proclaimed in 1931
JONS and Jose Antonio's movement merge into the Falange in 1934
July 1936 military rising led from Morocco turns into civil war
Worker collectivization of industry and farms in Catalonia and Aragon
Comintern organizes the International Brigades; long segment on volunteers
Condor Legion bombing campaign in the Basque country, Guernica
Republican surrender in April 1939; Badajoz bullring massacre described

notes: Primary subjects are the movement and the war, so roles are empty. Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera has a real segment but was kept in keywords to stay within five subjects. Covered span starts at the 1898 imperial collapse; earlier Carlist wars and Reconquista are background. The Trump/January 6 comparisons are framing, not story. The transcript places the gassing at Tangier; historically it was mainly the Rif.
